title: Ballot Buddy · North Carolina

boxes.title: How to read this
boxes.html: This report does not tell you who to vote for. It lays out who wrote the checks and what the public record shows. A donation is a fact about the donor; it is not proof of what the candidate will do.

footer: Sources. Who ran and who won: the Nov 3, 2026 results in the Results tab. Federal money: FEC bulk files, downloaded Nov 2, 2026. Records and positions: linked per item. North Carolina state-race money isn't in the guide yet, so those candidates have no money meters.

cands.bio: Attorney from Nash County, North Carolina. Practiced law for about 18 years, served in the NC House (1987-91) and NC Senate (1991-2001, majority leader from 1997), was Attorney General (2001-2017), then Governor (2017-2025). Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in 2026.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists endorsements of Cooper's 2026 campaign from Gov. Josh Stein, former Vice President Kamala Harris, Attorney General Jeff Jackson, the National Education Association, the North Carolina AFL-CIO, End Citizens United, the League of Conservation Voters Action Fund and Sierra Club North Carolina.
Former U.S. Rep. Wiley Nickel withdrew from the Democratic Senate primary in July 2025 and endorsed Cooper.

cands.gaps: We found no record of Cooper's positions on a statewide data-center ban, homestead property tax elimination, limits on investor or foreign buyers of homes and land, growth limits, Second Amendment issues, or police pay and pensions. His 2026 campaign site says data centers should pay the full cost of the power they use and that large tech companies should be encouraged to build their own energy sources, but it takes no position on banning or pausing data centers. We found no stated development stance, no documented controversies, and no foreign ties in the pages reviewed. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. The Ballotpedia and Wikipedia pages were cut off partway through, so some sections went unread.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His 2020 campaign website said he pushed the Republican legislature to a 9.5% teacher raise during his first term and called for better teacher pay and classroom funding.

cands.bio: Lawyer and Republican operative. Worked as a Department of Energy deputy assistant secretary and as chief of staff to Sen. Elizabeth Dole. Lobbyist at HBW Resources and executive at Consumer Energy Alliance. Chaired the North Carolina Republican Party (2019–2024) and the Republican National Committee (2024–2025).

endorsements.text: Endorsed by President Donald Trump and Vice President J.D. Vance.

cands.gaps: We found no record of Whatley's positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or institutional ownership of homes and land, growth and land conservation, school choice or teacher pay, or taking money from foreign-linked or big donors. He has never held elected office, so there are no legislative actions to cite. His campaign site gives general statements on immigration, policing, guns and abortion, but no specific bills or plans. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. Sources differ on whether his Department of Energy title was 'principal deputy assistant secretary' or 'deputy assistant secretary', and we could not confirm which. We could not independently verify his exact move date to North Carolina beyond the 'early high school years' reported by Wikipedia.

platform.summary: This is the platform Ballot Buddy scores against, adapted to North Carolina. James Fishback ran on it in the 2026 Republican primary for Florida governor: an affordability and land-protection message on top of a conservative base. Details that only applied to Florida have been swapped for North Carolina. It's one yardstick, chosen by this guide, and not a neutral one.

planks.title: Ban data centers statewide
planks.promise: Ban AI and hyperscale data centers in every North Carolina county through statewide preemption of county approvals, to protect farmland, water and electric bills.
planks.tells_for: Votes or stated positions to ban, put a moratorium on, or preempt data-center approvals; opposing data-center rezonings on farmland; refusing data-center-industry money.
planks.tells_against: Votes to approve or fast-track a data center, rezone farmland for one, or give it tax breaks; campaigning on attracting data centers or AI infrastructure.

planks.title: Eliminate homestead property taxes
planks.promise: Eliminate property taxes on North Carolina residents' primary homes (not second homes, short-term rentals or mega-estates), paid for by rolling local government spending back.
planks.tells_for: Votes for homestead exemption increases, assessment caps or abolition; pledges to cut or end homestead taxes; pledges to cut local spending or tax rates.
planks.tells_against: Votes or statements for raising property taxes; opposing homestead tax relief; defending local government revenue growth.

planks.title: North Carolina homes and land for North Carolinians
planks.promise: Ban private equity and Wall Street firms from buying single-family homes, tax out-of-state vacation-home buyers, and keep foreign adversaries from owning North Carolina land.
planks.tells_for: Supporting limits on institutional or foreign buyers of homes and land; proposing taxes or caps on out-of-state or investor purchases.
planks.tells_against: Opposing limits on corporate or foreign land buying; courting institutional or foreign real-estate capital.

planks.title: Slow growth, protect land and water
planks.promise: Develop slower and smarter, stop overdevelopment, and conserve North Carolina's state parks, waterways and natural lands.
planks.tells_for: Votes or statements to hold or tighten growth limits, require approvals for large developments, deny rezonings of farmland or open space, fund conservation; refusing developer money.
planks.tells_against: Votes to expand development boundaries, waive development oversight, preempt local growth limits, approve large developer land deals over resident objections; heavy developer funding.

planks.title: North Carolina workers first: end H-1B
planks.promise: End H-1B abuse with fines that wipe out any savings from replacing a North Carolina worker, keep H-1B workers off state contracts, raise foreign-student tuition, and back strong immigration enforcement and deportations.
planks.tells_for: Votes or statements for state cooperation with federal immigration enforcement, E-Verify, detention of criminal illegal immigrants, limiting H-1B or guest-worker displacement of Americans.
planks.tells_against: Votes or statements against immigration-enforcement bills; defending H-1B or guest-worker expansion or sanctuary-style policies.

planks.title: No foreign or big-donor money
planks.promise: Refuse contributions from foreign-affiliated groups (naming AIPAC) and run against donor capture.
planks.tells_for: Stated pledges to refuse foreign-linked, corporate-PAC, developer or out-of-state big-donor money; small-dollar funded campaigns.
planks.tells_against: Documented reliance on developer, foreign-linked or mega-donor or PAC money; stated openness to it.

planks.title: Back police, restore order
planks.promise: Raise pay and improve pensions for law enforcement and corrections officers, charge teen takeovers as felonies, surge state resources on homelessness, and remove prosecutors who refuse to prosecute.
planks.tells_for: Votes or positions raising penalties for rioting or disorder, funding or improving pay and pensions for officers, supporting police, tough-on-crime prosecution.
planks.tells_against: Votes cutting officer pensions or benefits; opposing penalties for public disorder; defund-style positions.

planks.title: Defend the Second Amendment
planks.promise: Eliminate Red Flag laws, end restrictions on suppressors, bump stocks and forced-reset triggers, and oppose raising gun purchase ages; also pull Flock cameras and stop Palantir contracts.
planks.tells_for: Votes for permitless carry and stand-your-ground, against red-flag laws and new purchase-age limits; pledges to oppose new gun restrictions.
planks.tells_against: Votes for red-flag laws, purchase-age or waiting-period laws, assault-weapon or magazine limits.

planks.title: Pro-life, no exceptions
planks.promise: Life begins at conception; shut down North Carolina's abortion clinics and replace them with crisis pregnancy centers, plus paid maternity leave.
planks.tells_for: Votes or statements for abortion bans, waiting periods or other abortion restrictions; support for pregnancy centers.
planks.tells_against: Votes or statements against abortion restrictions; support for abortion-access measures.

planks.title: School choice and teacher pay
planks.promise: Universal school choice funded toward parity with public schools, a state homeschool commissioner, and a 25% raise for teachers.
planks.tells_for: Votes or statements for vouchers, charters or universal choice and for raising teacher pay.
planks.tells_against: Votes or statements against voucher or charter expansion or school-choice funding.
